digest.component_or_area: store write lock / mkdir lock reclamation
propositions: On platforms without /proc (macOS), _process_start_time always returns None, making the recycled-pid discriminant unsatisfiable and causing _mkdir_lock_is_stale to return False indefinitely when a dead process's pid is recycled by an unrelated live process, creating an unbounded wedge

The fix applies _mkdir_lock_age_exceeds_ceiling on the live-pid branch only when current_start is unavailable (None), bounding the orphan case to 1h while preserving the never-on-timer-alone guarantee for genuinely live owners with matching start times

The owner-identity and lock reclamation logic was refactored from lock.py (798 LOC) into a new lock_owner.py module to satisfy the 800-LOC module-size limit, with lock.py reaching all moved names module-qualified to maintain a single binding for monkeypatch correctness

A dead holder whose recycled pid collides with an unrelated live process is now reclaimed once past the ceiling rather than wedging indefinitely, verified on macOS where the no-/proc branch is exercised

The dual-leg invariant (fcntl lock held for entire lifetime of mkdir lock) ensures reaching _mkdir_lock_is_stale proves the stamped owner already let go, so the ceiling only fires on orphans and cannot break a genuinely live owner
